claims.statement: Runnable documentation examples are authored in supported-language files under `src/code-samples/`; `src/code-samples-generated/` is a gitignored extraction intermediate and snippet MDX is generated from the source rather than hand-authored.

The extractor is line based and recognizes language-specific `:snippet-start:`/`:snippet-end:` and `:remove-start:`/`:remove-end:` comment markers, strips remove regions, dedents snippet bodies, and fails on unclosed snippet or remove markers.

Snippet IDs need the language suffix `-py`, `-js`, `-java`, `-kt`, `-go`, or `-sh`, because the MDX generator maps that suffix to an output language and skips an extracted snippet whose ID does not end in the expected suffix.

TypeScript samples execute as a single module, so their visible regions and remove blocks share module scope; independently runnable snippets with duplicate imports or top-level bindings must be split into separate files.

The sample runner accepts an explicit supported file list or recursively selects eligible samples, executes Python, TypeScript, Java/Kotlin, Go, and shell through their language toolchains, and defaults each invocation timeout to 1,200 seconds.

Ordinary sample failures, timeouts, and trace-collection exceptions fail the runner, but a detected LangSmith 429 rate limit is retried three total times with 15-second delays and is then reported as skipped rather than failed.

`make code-snippets` runs extraction followed by MDX generation; a full extraction clears supported intermediates and rebuilds them, while `CODE_SNIPPET_SOURCES` replaces intermediates only for selected valid source stems but MDX generation still scans all existing intermediates.

MDX generation emits language fences, consumes optional code-group presentation markers, and expands the first eligible Python or TypeScript model ID and repeated matching occurrences into seven-provider CodeGroups; `KEEP MODEL`, embedding IDs, and models passed to embeddings or provider-specific chat constructors remain unexpanded so the resulting sample stays runnable, and a trace CTA is appended only when the manifest supplies a URL.

With tracing enabled, only a successful source file containing exactly one snippet marker can receive a public trace link; the collector polls for a recent agent-like root run, shares it, and records metadata in `trace-links.json`, while multi-snippet files are recorded as skipped and stale single-snippet entries are removed.

The Test Code Samples workflow skips fork PR sample execution, tests changed eligible sample files on internal PRs and all samples on manual or monthly runs, and enables tracing only for manual or scheduled full runs.

After a successful traced full run and regeneration, CI updates or creates the deterministic `chore/refresh-code-sample-traces` pull request only when the trace manifest or generated snippet MDX differs; a separate observer creates a Linear issue only for failed or cancelled scheduled sample runs.

Public trace sharing is an explicit publication operation: `make update-code-sample-traces` enables tracing, uses the configured or default `docs-code-samples` project, runs samples, then regenerates MDX; it requires `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`.

Go code samples share the `src/code-samples` module: `go.mod` declares module dependencies and Go 1.25.0, `go.sum` locks their checksums, the runner invokes `go run` from that directory, and CI derives its Go setup from that module file.

Python samples run in the repository's uv environment, while TypeScript samples share `src/code-samples/package.json` and its lockfile; the Make targets install that package before executing TypeScript samples.

TypeScript sample provider strings must use `google:` rather than Python-only `google_genai:`, while Python samples must retain `google_genai:`; the generator's Google CodeGroup variants intentionally use those language-specific keys.

The shared TypeScript sample package declares and locks `@langchain/mcp-adapters` at 2.0.0, so the MCP adapter 2 examples resolve the same adapter implementation and Model Context Protocol dependency family from `src/code-samples/`.

`mcp-elicitation.ts` turns a server input request into a LangGraph interrupt, resumes the pending interrupt with `createMCPElicitationResume` using the server request key, and its local remove-region harness verifies the interrupted and resumed booking path before closing adapter and server resources.

`mcp-shared-adapter.ts` uses a module-scoped adapter and refresh-mode tool listing; its local harness verifies concurrent calls share a client, unchanged listings reuse tool wrappers, and closing the adapter invalidates an earlier wrapper.

`mcp-tool-errors.ts` documents two error contracts: an MCP `isError` response becomes an error-status `ToolMessage` when invoked as a tool call, while direct invocation rejects; its local calculator fixture asserts both outcomes and closes all resources.

The MCP quickstart always closes its adapter, validates that the documentation server exposes tools and that agent construction succeeds, and deliberately skips the live model invocation when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unavailable.

The focused MDX-generator test rejects TypeScript `google_genai:` and legacy `google_search` usage, requires Python samples to retain `google_genai:`, and checks that both the declared and lockfile-resolved `@langchain/google` version meet the minimum for mixed built-in and function tools.
